records.definition: An enclosed internal structural void or microcavity buried within the tertiary core of a globular protein without direct bulk-solvent tunnel access, occurring either as an apolar empty packing defect or as a partially polar microcavity occupied by ordered structural water molecules that modulate core packing density, compressibility, and conformational stability.

An internal molecular tunnel connecting two spatially separated catalytic active sites within a bifunctional enzyme or multienzyme complex (such as carbamoyl phosphate synthetase, tryptophan synthase, glucosamine-6-phosphate synthase, or glutamine phosphoribosylpyrophosphate amidotransferase) that directly translocates a reactive metabolic intermediate (such as nascent ammonia or indole) from the donor active site to the acceptor active site while sequestering it from bulk solvent.

assessment: No identity collision. Enclosed hydration void lacks direct bulk-solvent tunnel access; lateral fenestration traverses channel wall to lipid exterior. Intermediate-channeling tunnel joins catalytic sites with asserted function; a bottleneck is a minimum-radius region of a path. These neighboring records were read solely for boundary discrimination, not scientifically audited or endorsed.
